summary:
For the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, our team (DreamLabs) developed Space-Ready, a web-based continuous ground health monitoring and readiness drift-detection application designed for the 2-to-4-year pre-mission astronaut training window. 

To address the blind spots between NASA's infrequent formal clinical exams—where over 99.7% of training days lack standardized lifestyle tracking—we translated NASA OCHMO standards into a structured 30-question weekly checkup across six core pillars: Sleep, Nutrition, Exercise, Stress, Social Connection, and Recovery. After locking an astronaut’s personalized baseline during Weeks 1–4, our engine tracks weekly drift, applies 3-week temporal smoothing to filter noise, triggers tiered early-warning alerts before performance reaches NASA's critical -20% decrement threshold, prescribes targeted countermeasures, and compiles 52-week annual rollups for L-60 flight certification.

This tool is vital because NASA’s active astronaut corps has contracted to 44 members, shrinking operational safety margins to 15% and leaving virtually zero crew redundancy. By replacing 3–4 isolated checkpoints with over 100 longitudinal data points, Space-Ready prevents late mission disqualifications and establishes clean ground baselines so flight surgeons can accurately distinguish microgravity effects from pre-existing habits during orbit.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Our team (Team DreamLabs) developed Space-Ready, a web-based continuous ground health monitoring and readiness drift-detection application designed around the 2-to-4-year pre-mission astronaut training window. Each week, astronauts complete a focused 30-question checkup across six core spaceflight pillars: Sleep, Nutrition, Exercise, Stress, Social Connection, and Recovery. Each question is scored on a 0–4 risk gradient and converted into an intuitive 0–100% readiness score. During Weeks 1–4, Space-Ready calibrates and permanently locks an astronaut’s personal baseline composite score. Every week thereafter, our engine applies a 3-week trailing rolling average to Sleep and Stress to filter out short-term biological noise, computes a weighted composite score (with Recovery weighted at 0.8x and all other pillars at 1.0x), and measures readiness drift against the locked baseline. Status is classified into four alert tiers—Green (≤ 5 pts), Yellow (6–15 pts), Orange (16–20 pts), and Red (> 20 pts)—automatically isolating the lowest-scoring pillar and prescribing a targeted, NASA-aligned countermeasure whenever drift occurs. Multi-year 52-week annual rollups verify whether average drift stays within 5 points to earn L-60 Preflight Certification, and users can export complete JSON or CSV telemetry logs.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Between NASA's 3 to 4 formal preflight clinical exams, over 99.7% of training days lack standardized lifestyle readiness tracking—allowing silent cortisol accumulation, circadian fragmentation, or missed strength loading to go unnoticed until right before launch. Space-Ready replaces those few isolated snapshots with 104 to 208 longitudinal weekly data points. With NASA’s active astronaut corps contracted to 44 members and operational safety margins down to 15%, there is virtually zero crew redundancy across Artemis, ISS Commercial Crew, and Starliner missions. Our intended impact is twofold: first, to catch subtle lifestyle erosion at just 5 points of drift so flight surgeons and trainers have months of runway to intervene before hitting NASA's critical -20% mission pause threshold; and second, to provide clean, continuous preflight ground baselines so in-orbit medical teams can accurately distinguish microgravity effects from pre-existing ground habits.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

We built Space-Ready as a full-stack TypeScript web application. On the frontend, we used React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8, and Tailwind CSS v4, paired with Chakra Petch, Inter, and JetBrains Mono aerospace typography. Deterministic application state, weekly scoring history, baseline locking, and alert logic are managed using Zustand with localStorage persistence. For data visualization and user experience, we used Recharts for interactive longitudinal trend graphs, Lucide React and Motion for UI iconography and animations, and PDFKit for report exports. On the backend, we built a Node.js and Express server (server.ts) integrating the @google/genai SDK (gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image) with dotenv environment management. We also utilized Google AI Studio and Google Gemini models for coding assistance, UI copy refinement, and generating optimized WebP/JPG aerospace visual assets.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

Rather than treating NASA guidelines as static reference text, we creatively engineered published NASA standards—specifically OCHMO-STD-100.1A, OCHMO-TB-031, NASA OIG Report IG-22-007, and NASA Human Research Program (HRP) frameworks—directly into our mathematical scoring engine, alert boundaries, and L-60 certification rules. In designing Space-Ready, our team carefully considered biological hysteresis (why sleep debt and stress require 3-week rolling averages rather than single-week spikes), the "exam-cramming" effect where astronauts temporarily peak before scheduled physicals, individual physiological differences (solved by locking a personalized 4-week baseline rather than enforcing a rigid one-size-fits-all score), and operational schedule risk caused by today’s smaller astronaut corps.
dataRefs: NASA Office of Inspector General Report IG-22-007
